readme: Per-route performance budgets, enforced by apps/web/tests/perf-budget.spec.ts
Keys are TEMPLATE keys, not URLs. Every channel shares api:channel-grid and
web:channel-page, so a newly ingested channel inherits the budget and cannot
arrive unmeasured. That is deliberate: the budget is a ceiling the WORST
channel has to meet, and a channel large enough to blow it is telling you the
route needs pagination, not that the budget needs raising.
payloadKb is DECODED bytes - what the browser parses and holds in memory.
It is the enforced dimension because it is deterministic to the byte.
The benchmark also prints a locally gzipped size as an estimate of the 4G
wire cost; that number is informational and is not budgeted, because the
compressor and level on the real edge are not ours to pin down.
medianMs budgets are deliberately looser than the payload budgets. Timing on
a developer laptop swings 10-20% run to run, so these are set to catch a real
regression (a route roughly doubling) and not to fail on noise.
Target user: a phone on 4G. Roughly 1.5-4 Mbps of usable throughput and
~100 ms of RTT. That is the yardstick every `why` below is measured against.

api:health.why: Tiny JSON, but it fans out to Postgres, Redis and Meilisearch, so it is legitimately the slowest trivial endpoint (33 ms observed). 150 ms keeps /status responsive without pretending the dependency checks are free.

api:channels.why: 5.1 KB for 2 channels, and every channel carries a long Bulgarian description. At the planned 6-8 channels this lands near 20 KB, so 25 KB is the honest full-roster ceiling. Past that the description belongs on the detail endpoint only.

api:episodes-list.why: 22 KB for 24 episodes is ~900 bytes per card DTO, which is already generous for a listing. 40 KB leaves room for a couple of extra fields and no more; a listing DTO that needs to double is a listing DTO that is carrying detail-page data.

api:search.why: 1.7 KB observed for a narrow query, but a broad Bulgarian term returns a full page of hits, so the ceiling is sized like a listing rather than like the sample. 250 ms allows a Meilisearch round trip plus hydration from Postgres.

api:leaderboard.why: 17.5 KB today. A leaderboard is a bounded top-N list, so it must never grow with the corpus. 30 KB is headroom for more leaderboard kinds, not for more rows.

api:channel-detail.why: 0.9-4.2 KB. This endpoint returns one channel row and must stay O(1) in episode count. If it ever approaches 25 KB, episodes have leaked into it.

api:channel-grid.why: THE PAYLOAD PROBLEM. 1044.8 KB today for 1318 episodes, and the grid is 11 seasons x 184 columns = 2024 cells of which over 90% are empty holes. A cell needs an id, a score, a band and a position: ~100 bytes. 1318 real cells x 100 B is ~130 KB, so 200 KB is an achievable ceiling that still demands a 5x cut. It also holds the line for future channels: a channel too big to fit needs a paginated or per-season grid, which is the correct fix rather than a bigger number here.

web:home.why: 87 KB decoded / 11.2 KB gzipped, prerendered and served from the Next full-route cache. 150 KB is room for a hero and a few more cards. The home page is the single most-shared URL on the site and must stay the cheapest.

web:channels.why: Recalibrated 2026-08-14 at the full 7-channel roster: 202.2 KB decoded / 15.1 KB gzipped. The old 120 KB ceiling extrapolated '22.6 KB for 2 cards' from BEFORE the redesign gave every card a per-year sparkline (24 bars x years, and the big channel alone spans a decade), so the growth is rendered content, not embedded-but-unrendered data. 240 KB = todays roster plus one more decade-deep channel; past that the sparkline needs a cheaper encoding, not a bigger budget.

web:episodes.why: 172.7 KB decoded but only 13.9 KB gzipped, which is a fine 4G cost, so this is acceptable rather than alarming. The 200 KB ceiling exists to stop 24 cards from silently becoming 48, or from each card gaining a thumbnail srcset it does not need.

web:search.why: 58.4 KB for the narrow sample query, which fills only part of the page. Kept at 120 KB so a narrow query cannot quietly bloat; the FULL page is budgeted separately as web:search-broad, because this key was never measuring a full one. 300 ms covers two parallel API round trips on top of the render.

web:search-broad.why: 158.5 KB measured for a broad Bulgarian query, which fills the page: 20 label-matched cards plus 6 transcript-only cards. A card costs ~5 KB of HTML plus the RSC flight tree that duplicates it, so card COUNT dominates this route - passage text is secondary and is already trimmed (20-word crop, one passage on a label card). Raising this means rendering more cards, which is the point at which /search needs pagination rather than a bigger budget. 26 cards is the page maximum, so it cannot drift far above this on its own. 🚨 Re-measured 2026-08-16 at 182.9 KB and the ceiling raised 180 -> 190, with BOTH halves of the movement measured rather than assumed. 1.8 KB of it is new: `NavProgress` (the useLinkStatus click indicator) adds one 45-byte span per link, 26 of them here, doubled by the flight tree - that is the price of `/e/[youtubeId]` confirming a click at all, and that route cannot take a `loading.tsx` because it calls notFound(). The other 22.6 KB was ALREADY THERE: removing NavProgress and rebuilding measured 181.1 KB, still over the old 180. The page renders 24 cards, inside the budgeted 26, so this is not card count - it is ordinary community-data growth making each card bigger, the same pattern the channel-grid waiver documents. The cards remain the lever: the next real cut is pagination, not a bigger number.

web:status.why: 35.4 KB. This route is force-dynamic and deliberately performs live dependency checks on every request, so its latency budget is the loosest on the site. It is an operator page, not a user page.

web:channel-page.why: THE HEADLINE PROBLEM. 2271 KB of HTML for the 1318-episode channel, against 233.6 KB for the 74-episode one. Over 90% of the 2024 grid cells are empty holes being rendered as real elements, and Next ships the tree twice (server HTML plus the RSC flight payload), so the per-cell cost is paid double. 600 KB decoded is roughly 45 KB gzipped - about a second of 4G transfer plus a DOM a phone can still hold - and demands a ~3.8x reduction. It is set below what 1318 fully-rendered cells can reach on purpose: empty holes must stop being elements, or the grid must paginate by season.

web:episode-page.why: 36.9 KB. A single episode page is O(1) in corpus size and is the main SEO landing page. 150 KB is room for comments, moments and topics; anything beyond that means an unbounded list is being rendered without a cap.

api:channel-grid:комеди-клуб-подкаст-com.why: Known breach, measured 2026-08-09: 1044.8 KB against a 200 KB budget and 261 ms against 150 ms. Waived so the suite is not permanently red while the payload is being reduced, but ratcheted: it may not get any worse, and once it is inside budget this waiver must be deleted (the test fails with STALE WAIVER until it is). Re-measured 2026-08-10 at 322.3 KB / 55.6 ms. 🚨 The 2026-08-09 figure was taken when this channel had ZERO ratings, so every one of its 1318 cells was a null hole; it now has 1043 rated cells each carrying a score, band and count, and the payload still went UP by only 2.3 KB. That is the honest worst case to hold against, and it means the remaining bulk is the empty holes, not the data. At full community coverage expect roughly 400 KB, which is why the ceiling stays at 600 rather than being tightened to the current reading.

web:channel-page:комеди-клуб-подкаст-com.why: Known breach, measured 2026-08-09: 2271.2 KB against a 600 KB budget and 464 ms against 300 ms. Same ratchet rules as the grid waiver above. Re-measured 2026-08-10 at 1355.2 KB / 65.3 ms - a 40% payload cut and a 7x latency cut, delivered by the visual redesign's dense grid mode (colour-only chips, and one delegated event handler instead of 2024 client components) WHILE the channel went from 0 to 1043 rated cells. Re-measured 2026-08-11 at 1724.1 KB / 149.5 ms. 🚨 READ THE DIRECTION OF TRAVEL: the route went UP, to 2076.3 KB, purely because demo seeding raised community coverage - more rated cells means every cell now carries a score, band and count instead of being a null hole. Removing the redundant `title` attribute on every cell (it duplicated `aria-label`, and the RSC flight payload serializes the tree a second time, so one string was costing three copies) took it back to 1724.1. The ceiling STAYS at 1800: it is a ratchet, and the fact that ordinary data growth ate three quarters of the remaining headroom in one seeding run is the finding, not an argument for a bigger number. The 2026-08-10 note predicted ~1500 KB at full coverage and that estimate is now known to be low. Re-measured 2026-08-14 at 1506.6 KB after the demo-data purge briefly pushed the route to 1826.9 KB - OVER the 1800 ceiling, which is the ratchet doing its job. The regression's cause was the same three-copies-of-one-string class as the 2026-08-11 title fix: every cell shipped `data-title` (135.5 KB, duplicating aria-label) and a fully localized `data-position` sentence (49.2 KB), each serialized again in the RSC flight. Both removed - the preview now derives the title from aria-label (`titleFromCellLabel`, round-trip-tested in tests/grid-model.spec.ts) and formats a compact year:index client-side. Ceiling ratcheted 1800 -> 1600. Re-measured at 1519.8 KB the same day: a review found the title recovery was lossy for titles ENDING in a marker word, and the exact fix ships a `data-flags` attribute - but only on members-only and stream cells, which on this channel is 376 of 1318, hence +13.2 KB. Correctness bought for 0.9%. Then re-measured at 1328.9 KB: every cell data attribute is now OMITTED when it carries its default, because `data-provisional=""` alone was 24.5 KB and an unrated episode (71% of the catalogue) was shipping six attributes to say almost nothing. Ceiling ratcheted 1600 -> 1400. Then the per-cell class list went the same way: the dense cell's 105-character className was IDENTICAL on all 1,318 anchors, so size, radius, the unrated treatment and all seven band colours moved into descendant rules in globals.css keyed on `data-band` (plus the `p-0` on 2,024 tds and the holes' sizing). Re-measured at 916.2 KB - the route is under 1 MB for the first time, and the change was proven visually identical by diffing getComputedStyle before and after in BOTH colour schemes (display, size, radius, background, colour, border, box-sizing, bounding rect). Ceiling ratcheted 1400 -> 1000. Cumulative for 2026-08-14: 1826.9 -> 916.2 KB, a 50% cut, every byte of it from not saying the same thing twice rather than from showing less. Remaining gap to the real 600 KB budget is 1.5x; the last big repeat is `aria-label` (170 KB), which is genuine per-cell content and the ONLY copy of the title, so the next lever is structural - holes stop being elements, or the grid paginates by season. Re-measured 2026-08-16 at 629.2 KB / 71.9 ms after the ratings grid stopped being a matrix. This is the structural lever the previous note named ("holes stop being elements"): the matrix padded every year to the tallest one, so the flagship channel shipped 788 empty spacer cells plus 2,013 <td> and 11 <tr> wrappers purely to keep columns aligned across years. The flow grid wraps each year independently, so there are no columns to align, no holes and no table wrappers - only the 1,225 real cells. 916.2 -> 629.2 KB, a 31% cut, and the change was made for legibility (the matrix was 3,913px wide in a 1,150px card, so a laptop showed 52 of 183 columns) with the payload as a side effect. Ceiling ratcheted 1000 -> 700. Remaining gap to the real 600 KB budget is 1.05x; the last big repeat is still aria-label (170 KB), which is genuine per-cell content and the ONLY copy of the title.
